sources.quote: small businesses are roughly 98 percent of Canadian employer businesses
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
sources.title: Key Small Business Statistics 2025
sources.evidence: As of December 2024, there were 1.10 million employer businesses in Canada, of which 1.08 million (98.2%) were small businesses, 16,953 (1.5%) were medium-sized businesses, and 3,380 (0.3%) were large businesses.

sources.quote: put online sales booked by Canadian retailers at a small single digit share of total retail
sources.title: The Daily — Retail trade, November 2025
sources.evidence: On a seasonally adjusted basis, retail e-commerce sales decreased 2.8% to $4.0 billion in November, accounting for 5.7% of total retail trade, compared with 6.0% in October. In December 2024 retail e-commerce sales accounted for 6.1% of total retail trade.

sources.quote: You need an approved Merchant Center account, Google Business Profile locations verified and matched to it, a products feed plus a local product inventory feed
sources.title: Local inventory ads and free local listings overview - Google Merchant Center Help
sources.evidence: The store code in your local inventory data source must match your Google Business Profile store codes. The item_id in the local inventory data source must align with the id in your primary product data source. All stores in your local product inventory feed must have matching published Business Profiles, and you must have a local brick and mortar business location where customers can physically visit.

sources.quote: Advertised prices must include every mandatory fee not imposed by government
sources.title: Drip pricing - Competition Bureau Canada
sources.evidence: Drip pricing involves offering a product or service at a price that is unattainable, because consumers must also pay additional non-government-imposed charges or fees to buy the product or service. Drip pricing is considered to be false or misleading under the law, unless the additional charges or fees are imposed by the government, such as sales tax. In 2022, the Government of Canada amended the Competition Act to explicitly recognize drip pricing as a deceptive business practice.

sources.quote: historically 98 percent Canadian direct costs for Product of Canada, 51 percent plus a qualifier for Made in Canada
sources.title: Made in Canada claims - Competition Bureau Canada
sources.evidence: The Competition Bureau will generally not challenge a claim that a good is a Product of Canada if at least 98% of the total direct costs of producing or manufacturing the good have been incurred in Canada and the last substantial transformation of the good occurred in Canada. Made in Canada claims are subject to a 51% threshold of Canadian content but should be accompanied by a qualifying statement such as Made in Canada with imported parts.

sources.quote: require French to be markedly predominant wherever a trademark or business name appears in another language
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française
sources.title: Entreprises : affichage des marques de commerce et des noms d’entreprises
sources.evidence: New rules concerning public signage and commercial advertising, particularly for business names and trademarks, have been in effect since June 1, 2025. A recognized trademark or business name entirely or partially in a language other than French that appears in signage visible from outside a premises must be accompanied by French terms that ensure clear predominance of French. For French to be clearly predominant, the French text must occupy at least twice as much space as text in another language and have visibility and readability at least equivalent.

sources.quote: Quebec's Consumer Protection Act bars expiry on gift card value
sources.publisher: Office de la protection du consommateur (Québec)
sources.title: Expiry Date - Prepaid Cards That May Be Used as Cash
sources.evidence: Merchants cannot indicate an expiry date on prepaid cards that can be used like cash. The amount you paid to purchase a card can never be lost because it has expired; as long as it has not been used, a card that was paid $50 will always keep its value. This rule has been in effect since June 30, 2010.

sources.quote: Contests need a skill testing question and prize disclosure under the Criminal Code and Competition Act
sources.title: Promotional Contests — Enforcement guidelines
sources.evidence: Section 74.06 of the Competition Act requires adequate and fair disclosure of the number and approximate value of the prizes, the areas to which they relate, and any fact within the knowledge of the person that affects materially the chances of winning. Criminal Code section 206 deals with contests and prohibits disposing of goods by any game of chance or mixed chance and skill in which the contestant pays consideration; when required, skill-testing questions should be included as important information relating to the chances of winning.
